purpose: Reuse the native import donor, graft selected pages, save with bounded native chunks and Blob output, propagate cancellation, and reuse the exact saved-revision cover.

method: Three rounds per task and revision; 27 full-donor sessions and 9 book plus selected-drawing-page sessions. Fresh browser each sample, sequential rotated variant order. No builds or independent validation during timing.
The same uninstrumented corpus-entry.ts is compiled against each checkout and its own SDK. File bytes are preloaded before the memory baseline; disk reads and file-picker interactions are excluded.

Import includes readable preview, hydration and registration. New PDFium retains one transient donor in the owner worker and hydrates/grafts only selected pages; prior revisions use their existing separate preview worker/source registration.

Export measures generation and worker response through each revision's production API. Blob assembly is included for exportPDFBlob. The separate download phase wraps legacy byte output without an extra slice. Persistent recent-file previews and filesystem sink completion are not timed.

PSS is Chromium process-tree proportional resident memory sampled every 50 ms, including native/WASM and Blob storage; it can miss short spikes. Export peak is the larger of plain and merged export peaks. Whole-workflow and download peaks remain separate.
The host had swap activity; per-round host counters and browser SwapPSS are retained. CPU-only Linux ARM64 Chromium measurements do not establish Tauri/WebView/GPU/Windows performance.

Independent validation uses pdf-lib for all page geometry, rotations, annotation/reply/link/field structures and edited metadata; Poppler compares text and 1200-pixel rasters on four original and three imported sampled pages.

The real corpus has no fillable fields. Selected widget/radio field relationships, link coordinates, exclusion of unselected page resources, rollback and encrypted save are covered separately by the native/application tests.
limitations: Pure export is slower than the previous PDFium byte-buffer path on these full documents (about 2% to 52%), while import plus merged export is faster. Chunking reduces peak memory and allows cancellation but is not a universal latency improvement.
The writer still rewrites the reachable PDF. True incremental append saving and complete removal of pdf-lib appearance/layout helpers are not implemented.

The working chunk targets 4 MiB or 8 ms at object boundaries. Graph discovery, encryption initialization, one large object and final xref work remain synchronous. Cold early cancellation took about 415 ms until worker readiness; mid-save checks took about 8 to 12 ms on the tested 1000-page drawing.
One persistent PDF per owner; opening an import chooser temporarily adds a second native donor in that same worker. It is released after commit/cancel. Separate editor tabs retain separate owners.
Blob storage retains the full output outside the native working buffer. The byte-array compatibility API and desktop write-file permission fallback can still materialize a full JS output array.
Imported source bytes are retained for undo/restoration. The native selected-page bank excludes unselected pages, but shared AcroForm resources are retained conservatively.

The PWA run recorded one revoked blob image request with ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND, no page errors, no visible broken images, one active worker and zero after closure. This resource cancellation remains visible in the raw evidence.
Visual checks sample the corpus; they do not prove every PDF/page is identical. Tauri frontend build and mocked filesystem tests do not establish native desktop runtime behavior.
